anatomy.flutter: SelectionControl is a real StatefulWidget shared by Checkbox/RadioGroupItem/Switch: it composes HitArea > Disabled > IgnorePointer > GestureDetector+MouseRegion > Focus > StateChangeFeedback > SizedBox > nested TweenAnimationBuilder(fill/border/ring) > Surface > Center(child) as one socket widget every control wears.
anatomy.web: There is no selection-control component file; the doc page's own comment says the row is composed from Field (FieldContent/FieldLabel/FieldTitle/FieldDescription) wrapping a standalone Checkbox or Switch, each under 80 lines and rendering only the control itself.
anatomy.note: The doc page states this is a deliberate decision, not an omission: 'Adding a SelectionControl would give the system two ways to build a selection row... The name is kept here so the shared capability stays findable; the implementation is the composition above.' Flutter centralizes the shared socket in one widget class; the web centralizes the shared row in Field, which every other form control already composes with, and reuses checkboxControlClassName/radioControlClassName string constants instead of a shared component for the control itself. Anatomy is not parallel by construction, and the doc page argues why the web mechanism is correct.

api.flutter: SelectionControl(width,height,radius,fill,border,shadow,duration,jellyState,child,onTap,enabled,disabledReason,inert,invalid,forceFocusRing,focusNode,skipTraversal,onKey,semantics) exposes ~15 low-level parameters that Checkbox/RadioGroupItem/Switch each supply.
api.web: There is no equivalent props surface to compare — Checkbox and Switch each take their own Radix props (checked/onCheckedChange/disabled etc.) and Field takes orientation/htmlFor wiring; no single API unifies them.
api.note: This mirrors the anatomy verdict: Flutter's API surface is the shared widget's constructor, and the web's equivalent 'surface' is a documented composition pattern (Field + a bare control) rather than a component with its own props, so there is no single API to hold to parity — the doc page names this explicitly as the intended shape.

states.flutter: _SelectionControlState tracks _focused locally and derives _enabled = enabled && !inert && onTap != null, _focusable = enabled && (inert || onTap != null), with three documented states (operable/inert/enabled:false) in the inert field's doc comment table.
states.web: checkbox.tsx and switch.tsx both carry data-[state=checked/unchecked/indeterminate], focus-visible:ring-3, aria-invalid:ring-3, disabled:opacity-50 (data-disabled:opacity-50 for switch), matching the rest/hover/focus/invalid/disabled matrix Field-composed controls document.
states.note: n/a is not used here because both sides genuinely implement the same state matrix (rest, focus-visible ring, checked/unchecked, invalid ring, disabled dimming); Flutter's extra 'inert' three-way split (operable/inert/disabled) reproduces a Radix-specific indeterminate-with-no-handler state that the web's own aria-invalid/disabled attributes already express, so this is recorded as a match rather than a gap.

disabled.flutter: SelectionControl.enabled=false routes through Disabled(disabled: !widget.enabled, reason: widget.disabledReason) and IgnorePointer, dimming via theme and taking the control out of the focus order via _focusable.
disabled.web: Checkbox's class list carries disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50 group-has-disabled/field:opacity-50, and Switch carries data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:opacity-50, both driven by the native/Radix disabled attribute which also removes the control from the tab order.
disabled.note: Both explain themselves visually (dimming) and both remove the control from the tab order when truly disabled; disabledReason on the Flutter side surfaces as a tooltip, which is the same recovery-context role a disabled Field's description text plays on the web.

interaction.flutter: SelectionControl._onKey wires Enter, numpadEnter and Space to widget.onTap when _enabled, and Focus(canRequestFocus: _focusable, skipTraversal: widget.skipTraversal) handles roving tabindex for RadioGroup.
interaction.web: Checkbox and Switch are Radix primitives rendered as native <button>s, which natively answer Enter/Space, Tab focus, and (for Radio, not shown here but documented on the doc page) arrow-key roving tabindex within a group.
interaction.note: Both platforms land on the same keyboard contract (Tab to focus, Space/Enter to toggle, arrow keys to rove within a radio group) even though Flutter wires it by hand with FocusNode/KeyEventResult and the web gets it from the native <button> element plus Radix's RadioGroup.

semantics.flutter: SelectionControl.semantics is applied inside the HitArea's expanded hit region so a Semantics wrapper is never rejected by an ancestor's bounds check; HitArea's own doc computes a 42x34 checkbox/radio target and 66x38 switch target from '-inset-x-3'/'-inset-y-2'-style insets measured off the padding box.
semantics.web: Checkbox's after:-inset-x-3 after:-inset-y-2 pseudo-element expander and Switch's identical after:-inset-x-3 after:-inset-y-2 (on a 44x24 h-6 w-11 track) match those exact insets, and both rely on FieldLabel's htmlFor to give the control its accessible name.
semantics.note: The Flutter doc comment itself flags that the checkbox/radio target measures 42x34, 2px short of the --size-target-min 44px floor per RULES §7 ('the checkbox misses it by 2px, at 42... That is what the reference renders') — this is a known, matched shortfall reproduced faithfully on both platforms rather than a divergence between them, so semantics parity holds even though the underlying target-size rule is itself unmet on both sides.
